title: National Adoption Month, 2025
summary:
The White House has proclaimed November 2025 as National Adoption Month, highlighting the goal that every child should have a safe, permanent home and encouraging the public to support children waiting for families. The message underscores recent and past actions the administration says will make adoption and foster care stronger, and invites Americans to get involved.

According to the proclamation, families who adopt may see financial help through a more accessible adoption tax credit and an expanded child tax credit under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. It also points to the Family First Prevention Services Act as a major reform aimed at keeping families together when possible, and notes a new executive order focused on helping young people in or leaving foster care with tools to succeed as adults. The First Lady’s advocacy is cited as part of this effort.

Children in foster care, adoptive parents, kinship caregivers, and organizations that support them could benefit from added attention, potential funding, and simplified access to financial supports. States, local agencies, and community partners may also gain momentum to coordinate services that prevent unnecessary family separation and ease the transition to adulthood for foster youth.

At the same time, some may have concerns. If resources or reforms are unevenly implemented, families and children could face delays or gaps in support. Emphasis on adoption may worry those who prioritize family preservation, especially if services to stabilize birth families are limited. Others may question whether tax credits and executive actions will reach those with the greatest need or whether the focus and language of the proclamation fully reflects the diversity of families seeking to adopt. The proclamation closes by calling on all Americans to uplift children, support caregivers, and strengthen family and community ties throughout the month.
